objectives: Master virtual production: LED volumes + StageCraft + Unreal Engine + ICVFX.
Survey AI in cinematography: generative video, diffusion, ML rotoscoping + color.
Understand HDR delivery + IMAX expansion + streaming vs cinema + the future of the DP.

slides.title: Virtual production: StageCraft, LED volumes, Unreal Engine 5
slides.body:
**Virtual production** (VP) — real-time computer-graphics integrated with live-action capture — became the most consequential cinematography technology of the 2020s.

**The Mandalorian + Lucasfilm StageCraft** (2019, Disney+):
- Showrunner Jon Favreau + cinematographer **Greig Fraser** + **Baz Idoine** + **Industrial Light & Magic** + **Epic Games** (Unreal Engine) built the prototype LED volume in Manhattan Beach.
- **The Volume** — 270° wraparound LED wall ~ 75 ft diameter × 20 ft tall + ceiling. Roe Visual Black Pearl BP2v2 panels (~2.84 mm pixel pitch). Camera tracking via Mo-Sys + stYpe + similar. Unreal Engine renders the environment in real time at 24-30 fps, synced to camera shutter to avoid flicker.
- **Frustum rendering** — only the camera's view-frustum + an 'outer frustum' for light spill is rendered at full fidelity; the rest renders simpler to save GPU. As the camera tracks, the high-fidelity frustum follows.
- **ICVFX (in-camera VFX)** — final image is captured through the lens, in-camera, with the LED-projected environment + practical foreground actors + props. Eliminates greenscreen post-comp for most setups + lets actors see + react to the environment.
- *The Mandalorian* season 1 (8 episodes, 2019) — first big show using LED at scale. 50%+ shots in The Volume. Won the **2020 Primetime Emmy for Outstanding Special Visual Effects** + drove industry-wide adoption.
- *Mando* seasons 2 + 3 + *The Book of Boba Fett* + *Obi-Wan Kenobi* + *Ahsoka* — Volume-based.

**Other StageCraft + volume productions**:
- **Westworld** + **House of the Dragon** (HBO).
- *The Batman* (Fraser, 2022) — partial VP.
- **Maleficent: Mistress of Evil** (Henry Braham, 2019) — early volume experimentation.
- **The Lion King** (Caleb Deschanel, 2019) — entirely virtual but pre-volume; Favreau's VR-based virtual scouting precursor.
- **The Volume Toronto** (Pixomondo at CBS Stage 23) for *Star Trek: Discovery* + *Strange New Worlds*.
- **Eyeline Studios** + **Final Pixel** + **DNEG VP** + **NEP Virtual Studios** — multiple global vendors.

**Unreal Engine 5** (Epic Games, 2022+) — the dominant VP render engine. **Nanite** virtualized micropolygon geometry + **Lumen** real-time global illumination + **MetaHumans** — push the rendered photorealism close to film. Coupled with **nDisplay** + Volume vendor's stack for synchronized multi-projector rendering.

**Virtual scouting + previs**:
- **Virtual scouting** — director + DP + production designer don VR headsets + walk through the digital environment as if on location. Plan blocking + lensing + camera moves before any physical build.
- **Previs + postvis** — Halon, The Third Floor, Proof, Pixar's Brian Pope. Sketched animatics replacing storyboards for VFX-heavy sequences.
- **Techvis** — engineering pre-vis specifying camera moves, lens lengths, exact volume needs.
- **Simulcam** + **ARRI Live Compositor** — on-set real-time compositing of CGI elements into the camera viewfinder during shoot.

**Steve Yedlin + Virtual Production research**:
- Yedlin has written extensively at yedlin.net on virtual-production color management + the false-equivalence problem between volumes + traditional location shooting. Argues that virtual production's biggest limitation isn't dynamic range but **art-direction familiarity** — DPs + designers + directors haven't yet developed instincts for what plays vs what doesn't in volume work, the way they have for soundstage + location.

**Limits**:
- **Moiré** — LED-pixel + sensor / lens geometry can interact unfavorably. Fine pixel pitch (1.5 mm) helps but is expensive.
- **Dynamic range** — LED walls 5-7 stops vs sensor 15-17 stops. Bright daylight exteriors particularly tricky.
- **Wide-angle close-ups** — extreme wide lens may resolve the wall's flatness + reveal it as a wall.
- **Reflections** — chrome + glass props reflect the wall (sometimes useful, sometimes a giveaway).
- **Cost** — $50k-$200k/day rental for The Volume + similar facilities; not always cheaper than location, but predictable + weatherproof + faster reset between setups.

Virtual production won't replace location or studio. But it has joined them as a third major production environment + reshaped television-budget VFX delivery.

slides.title: AI in cinematography: generative video, ML tools, autonomous workflows
slides.body:
**Generative video models** (2022-2025) — diffusion + transformer hybrids producing short video clips from text or image prompts.

- **Runway Gen-1 / Gen-2 / Gen-3 Alpha / Gen-3 Alpha Turbo** (Runway ML) — earliest commercial video generators (2022-2024). Initially short (4-second) clips at low resolution. Gen-3 Alpha (2024) extends to 10-second 1280×768 with reasonable temporal coherence. Used for previs, mood boards, sometimes finishing.
- **Pika 1.0 / Pika Labs** — accessible web-based image-to-video + text-to-video.
- **Sora** (OpenAI, announced Feb 2024, released Dec 2024) — diffusion transformer producing up to 1 minute 1080p coherent video from text prompt. State-of-art temporal + spatial coherence + camera-move emulation. Restricted API access.
- **Veo / Veo 2 / Veo 3** (Google DeepMind, 2024-2025) — competitor to Sora. Veo 3 (announced 2025) includes synchronized audio generation.
- **Marey** (Moonvalley, 2025) — fully-licensed-training-data video model targeting cinema workflows. Pitched to studios as legally safer for VFX integration.
- **Stable Video Diffusion** (Stability AI) + **Kling** (Kuaishou) + **HunyuanVideo** (Tencent) + **Mochi-1** (Genmo) — open-source / open-weight competitors.

**Diffusion video architecture** (sketch): latent diffusion in spatial + temporal axes; DiT (Diffusion Transformer) backbones; text encoders + 3D VAE; rectified-flow training for cleaner sampling. Sora's technical report (Brooks + Peebles et al. 2024) outlines spacetime patches as the training unit.

**ML tools in production cinematography workflow** (the bigger near-term impact):

- **Wonder Studio** (Wonder Dynamics) — automatic CG-character integration: track + roto + light-match + body-track a CG character into live-action footage. Released 2023. Replaces multi-week traditional VFX integration with automated pass.
- **Runway / Adobe Firefly / DaVinci Resolve Neural Engine** — ML rotoscoping + sky replacement + object removal + super-resolution + relighting. Widely deployed in 2024-2025 production. **Magic Mask** in Resolve isolates subjects without manual roto.
- **ML color grading + color matching** — Colourlab AI, Lattice Pro, Resolve's Neural Engine color matching. Auto-balance shots within a sequence. Colorists use as starting point, not replacement.
- **iZotope RX / Cedar / Waves Clarity Vx** — ML-driven dialogue cleanup + noise reduction + dereverb. Transformed dialogue post.
- **Topaz Video AI** — AI upscaling + denoising + frame interpolation. Used on archival restoration + low-budget finishing.
- **Adobe Speech-to-Text + Premiere + Descript** — paper-edit workflow from transcripts; documentary editing transformed.
- **Depth estimation + LiDAR + neural radiance fields (NeRFs)** — Gaussian Splatting + NeRF capture for location preservation + virtual scouting. Used to digitize sets + locations for VP.
- **Auto-focus via LiDAR + ML** — DJI Ronin 4D + ARRI Trinity + cmotion LiDAR systems with neural-network subject tracking.

**Where AI helps + where it doesn't (2025)**:
- **Helps**: previs / mood boards / pitch-decks; VFX integration (Wonder Studio); rotoscoping + sky replacement + object removal; dialogue cleanup; upscaling; transcript-driven editing; LiDAR auto-focus; ML color matching.
- **Doesn't yet replace**: principal photography (no camera, no lensing); long-form coherent storytelling; precise actor performance; safety + craft of the physical set; the cinematographer's role.
- **Open ethical / labor issues**: training data + copyright (lawsuits ongoing 2024-2025); WGA + SAG-AFTRA 2023 strikes won AI protections; ASC + BSC + cinematographer guilds negotiating AI guidelines.

**The plausible near-term trajectory** (per Yedlin + others): AI augments + accelerates — VFX integration, color matching, mood boards, scene-extension, archival restoration. The DP's craft (lensing, lighting, composition, performance support, set politics) remains human + central. Generative video may become a viable replacement for stock-footage + b-roll within 2-3 years + may produce theatrical-quality short-form work, but feature-length human-acted cinema is not on a near-term replacement path.

slides.title: HDR delivery, IMAX expansion, streaming vs cinema, the DP's evolving role
slides.body:
**HDR (High Dynamic Range)** — display + delivery standards delivering wider dynamic range + wider color gamut than legacy Rec.709 SDR.

- **HDR10** — open standard, 10-bit, static metadata. Most TVs + streaming.
- **HDR10+** — Samsung-led dynamic metadata variant.
- **Dolby Vision** — proprietary 12-bit dynamic metadata. Most premium streaming + theatrical Dolby Cinema. Tone-mapping per-scene + per-display. The dominant premium HDR format.
- **HLG (Hybrid Log-Gamma)** — BBC + NHK; live broadcast HDR.
- **Peak nits** — SDR mastering: 100 nits. HDR mastering: 1000 / 4000 / 10000 nits target. Consumer displays: 600-2000 nits typical OLED/QLED.
- **DCI-P3 (theatrical) / Rec.2020 (broadcast)** — wide gamuts. ACES 2065-1 + AP1 (ACEScg) workflows handle round-trip.

**HDR practical impact on cinematography**:
- Highlight handling — DP must compose for both SDR + HDR delivery. Specular highlights in HDR can dominate; faces must be correctly placed in luminance.
- Multi-deliverable color trim — DI typically masters at HDR + trim-passes to SDR + Dolby Vision + theatrical.
- DPs increasingly engaged through delivery; colorist + DP collaboration extends into trims.

**IMAX expansion + large-format cinema**:
- **IMAX 70 mm 15-perf horizontal** ~ 11K equivalent resolution — the highest-res capture medium in practical use. *The Dark Knight* (Pfister, 2008), *Interstellar* (Hoyte van Hoytema, 2014), *Dunkirk* (van Hoytema, 2017), *Oppenheimer* (van Hoytema, 2023). Nolan + Tarantino + Mendes + Cuarón embraced 65/70 mm.
- **IMAX Laser** — modern projection (laser instead of xenon) for higher contrast + wider gamut. Premium-format theaters expanded globally 2018-2024.
- **Aspect ratio shifting** within films — *Oppenheimer*, *The Dark Knight Rises*, *Mission: Impossible – Fallout* shift between scope + 1.43 IMAX during sequences captured on different formats.
- **65 mm digital** — ARRI Alexa 65 (6.5K horizontal sensor) approximates IMAX format on digital — *The Revenant*, *Mission: Impossible – Fallout*, *House of Gucci*.

**Streaming vs cinema (2020-2025)**:
- **Netflix 4K HDR Dolby Vision Atmos** — premium streaming standard. *Roma* (Cuarón, 2018, B&W digital), *The Irishman* (Scorsese, Prieto, 2019), *Mank* (Fincher, Messerschmidt, 2020), *The Power of the Dog* (Campion, Goonan, 2021), *Glass Onion*, *Maestro*.
- **Apple TV+** + **Amazon Prime Video** + **Disney+** + **HBO Max / Max** — all 4K HDR/Dolby Vision standard.
- **Aspect ratios for streaming**: Storaro's 2:1 (Univisium) widely adopted by Netflix originals; 1.85 + 2.39 + 16:9 + 1.43 IMAX all in use.
- **Theatrical vs streaming windows** — theatrical exclusivity windows shrank from 90 days (pre-pandemic) to 45 + same-day (pandemic) + 45 days (post-pandemic). Pandemic + streaming-first releases reshaped distribution. Premium cinema (IMAX, Dolby Cinema, 70 mm engagements) remains theatrical-exclusive.
- **Tentpole event films** — *Avatar 2*, *Top Gun: Maverick*, *Oppenheimer*, *Barbie* — proved theatrical event cinema viable. Mid-budget studio drama largely moved to streaming.

**The DP's evolving role + 'long takes' renaissance**:
- *1917* (Mendes-Deakins 2019, apparent two single takes), *Birdman* (Iñárritu-Lubezki 2014, apparent single take), *Russian Ark* (Sokurov 2002, true single take). Long-take immersion is now a definable craft choice.
- **Olivia Wilde + DP Matthew Libatique** — *Don't Worry Darling* (2022). Wilde represents the new generation of director-led cinematography collaboration.
- **Greta Gerwig + Rodrigo Prieto** + **Yorick Le Saux** — *Little Women*, *Barbie*.
- **Sean Baker + DPs** — *The Florida Project* (Alexis Zabe, 2017, 35 mm), *Tangerine* (2015, iPhone 5S — proving any camera can produce theatrical-quality cinema), *Anora* (Drew Daniels, 2024 Cannes Palme d'Or). The democratization of cinematic tools — phones, Blackmagic Pocket, mirrorless cameras — has opened the craft beyond traditional industrial gatekeepers.

**Climate impact + sustainable production**:
- Average studio feature: ~3000-4500 tons CO₂e equivalent. Travel + transport + lighting power + sets + catering dominant.
- **BAFTA Albert** + **Sustainable Production Alliance** (Netflix, Amazon, Disney, Warner, Universal, Paramount, Sony, NBCU) — industry-wide standards for measurement + reduction.
- LED lighting reduces power vs HMI/tungsten by ~70%. Generators going Tier 4 + battery-hybrid + solar-supplemented (Mango Mobile Power, Volta).
- LED volumes reduce travel + location footprint (one volume can be many locations) — though the volume itself draws ~ 1+ MW.
- Digital workflows reduce film stock + transport but increase storage / cloud-compute energy.

**The future of the DP role** (consensus 2025):
- Lensing + lighting + composition remain irreducibly human + creative.
- Toolset expands: physical fixtures + LED volumes + virtual cameras + ML-assisted finishing.
- DPs become more involved in DI + HDR finishing + display-prep (Yedlin's argument).
- Sustainability + diversity + labor (post-2023 strikes) become structural concerns.
- Cinematography as a discipline remains a 130-year-old craft adapting to ever-faster technological change — the principles of light + composition + movement + time are stable; the tools are not. The next great DP is currently apprenticing on someone's set.

question.question: Plan a volume + traditional-set hybrid shoot for a sci-fi feature
question.goal: A feature has 30 days of scenes split: 12 days alien-planet exteriors, 8 days spaceship-interior practical sets, 6 days Earth city, 4 days character close-ups. Plan which days are volume + which are traditional.

steps.prompt: Which 12 days suit the volume best + why?

acceptedAnswers: alien-planet exteriors — fully designed environments, time-of-day matching, no location practicality

steps.reveal: **Alien-planet exteriors** (12 days) — perfect Volume use. Designed CG environment in Unreal, time-of-day controllable, no weather, no permits, no travel. Actors see + react to the environment; light spills realistically onto them; reflections work. *The Mandalorian* template.

steps.prompt: Which 8 days require traditional practical sets?

acceptedAnswers: spaceship interiors — practical sets needed for actor blocking, props, close-ups

steps.reveal: **Spaceship interiors** (8 days) — practical set construction. Tight interiors with props + controls + wallspaces actors interact with don't suit volume (wall flatness shows on wide close-ups + actors can't grab a CG button). Build the set, dress it, light it traditionally. *Star Trek* + *Alien* templates.

steps.prompt: What about the 6 days of Earth city?

acceptedAnswers: real location — Earth references are too familiar; volume struggles with bright daylight wide exteriors

steps.reveal: **Earth city** (6 days) — real location. Audiences are familiar enough with terrestrial cities that any volume imperfection (parallax limit, dynamic range, scale) reads as fake. Bright daylight exteriors are also where volume dynamic range struggles most. Real location locks the realism.

steps.prompt: How do you handle the 4 days of character close-ups?

acceptedAnswers: schedule them on the relevant matching environment day; close-ups can use practical lighting matched to either set or volume

steps.reveal: Schedule close-ups within each environment block — alien-planet close-ups on volume days (volume light wraps actor for natural integration), spaceship close-ups on set days, city close-ups on location days. Close-ups generally don't need wide-angle and don't reveal volume flatness — works in any environment.

acceptedAnswers: ACES color pipeline + virtual scouting + previs + on-set Unreal team + match-grading across volume/practical/location

steps.reveal: **ACES** color pipeline ensures volume + practical + location all hit the same final color space. **Virtual scouting** in VR previews volume sequences pre-shoot. **Previs / techvis** for sequences crossing environments (CG matte paintings extending the practical set into a volume horizon, etc.). On-set Unreal team (4-8 people) keeps the engine running. Colorist match-grades final DI across all three environment types so the audience reads one consistent world.

question.finalResult:
$$\boxed{\text{Alien exteriors: Volume; Ship interiors: Set; City: Location; Close-ups: matched}}$$

Volume is one of three production environments — choose by what each does well + match-grade the whole.

question.question: Which **generative video models** are leading at the cinema-quality frontier in 2025 + what is their current production role?
options: **Sora** (OpenAI, Dec 2024 release) + **Veo / Veo 3** (Google DeepMind, 2025) + **Runway Gen-3** + **Pika** + **Marey** (Moonvalley, fully-licensed training data) + open-weight **HunyuanVideo** (Tencent) + **Kling** (Kuaishou) + **Mochi-1** (Genmo). Diffusion-transformer (DiT) architectures with spacetime patches; up to ~1 minute coherent video at 1080p+ from text/image prompts. **Current role (2025)**: previs + mood boards + concept art + stock-footage replacement + b-roll generation. **Not yet replacing**: principal photography, long-form coherent storytelling, precise actor performance, theatrical-quality features. Used alongside ML rotoscoping + ML color matching + Wonder Studio CG-character integration. WGA + SAG-AFTRA 2023 strikes won AI protections; copyright + training-data lawsuits ongoing. Generative video augments + accelerates the workflow but the DP's craft (lensing, lighting, composition, performance support) remains human + central.
question.explanation: Sora (OpenAI, late 2024), Veo 3 (Google 2025), Runway Gen-3, Pika, Marey (Moonvalley), and open-weight HunyuanVideo + Kling + Mochi-1. DiT diffusion-transformer architectures producing up to ~1 min coherent 1080p video. Current production role: previs + mood boards + concept art + b-roll generation. Not yet replacing principal photography or feature-length storytelling. Strike protections + copyright lawsuits ongoing.

slides.workedSolution: Leading generative video models 2025: Sora (OpenAI), Veo 3 (Google), Runway Gen-3, Pika, Marey (Moonvalley), HunyuanVideo, Kling, Mochi-1. DiT architectures + spacetime patches; ~1 min coherent 1080p. Production role: previs, mood boards, b-roll. Not replacing principal photography or features. Strikes + copyright lawsuits ongoing.

question.question: Why does HDR + Dolby Vision delivery change how cinematographers compose + light?
question.prompt: Modern Netflix + Apple TV + Amazon delivery defaults to 4K HDR Dolby Vision (1000+ nits peak, Rec.2020 wide-gamut). Cinematographers must now master for both HDR + SDR. Explain (a) how HDR changes the perceptual weight of highlights + specular reflections + practical lights; (b) why a face composition luminance that 'works' in SDR may break in HDR (and vice-versa); (c) the multi-trim DI workflow (HDR master → Dolby Vision metadata → SDR trim) + the DP's expanded role in finishing; (d) why peak nits and dynamic range matter less than scene-by-scene tone-mapping choices.

question.question: **The Mandalorian** season 1 (2019) — the first major show to use an LED volume at scale — was photographed by which DPs (name both)?
question.hint: Fraser also shot *Dune* + *The Batman*; Idoine continued the show.

question.prompt: In ≤120 words, summarize the state of cinematography's frontier (2025) — virtual production + AI + HDR + delivery + sustainability + the DP's future role.
question.rubric: Mentions: (1) **virtual production** (Lucasfilm StageCraft + The Mandalorian 2019 + Unreal Engine 5 + Greig Fraser + Baz Idoine) now a third major production environment alongside location + soundstage; ICVFX eliminates greenscreen for many setups; (2) **AI / generative video** (Sora + Veo + Runway + Marey + open-weight) at previs / b-roll level + ML tools (Wonder Studio, iZotope RX, Resolve Magic Mask, ML color) widely deployed in finishing; (3) **HDR + Dolby Vision** + 4K + Rec.2020 wide-gamut now default delivery; cinematographers extend into multi-trim DI; (4) **IMAX expansion** + 70 mm + large-format digital (Alexa 65) — *Oppenheimer* (Hoyte van Hoytema, 2023) the modern peak; (5) **streaming + theatrical hybrid** delivery; Netflix Apple Amazon premium-format; (6) **sustainability** (BAFTA Albert, LED savings, hybrid power, volume vs travel); (7) **labor + AI protections** (WGA + SAG-AFTRA 2023 strikes); (8) **the DP role** — lensing + lighting + composition + performance support remain human + central, but the toolset + finishing role expand. The principles of light + composition + movement + time are stable; the tools change every decade. Cinematography remains a 130-year-old guild craft adapting to faster technological change.
